les: Die seepad na Indië, en die skepe wat volg
kaps_punt: Die reis van Da Gama VOC (Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie) reise

items.bewering: Na Dias se reis het die seepad na die Ooste nog net halfpad geloop.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Dutch settlement' (sahistory.org.za/article/dutch-settlement), calls the Cape a 'halfway stop' on the Europe-Asia route. Great-circle distances (1flt.com / airportdistancecalculator.com): Lisbon-Cape Town about 4 630 nm, Cape Town-Mombasa about 2 145 nm, Mombasa-Kochi about 2 360 nm. So Dias's furthest point (Great Fish River / Kwaaihoek, SAHO node/10799) is a little over half the route. The road metaphor maps correctly: a route known up to a point, with the rest still unknown. It implies no false mechanism. Checked fresh this round, as was every item below.

items.bewering: Portugal wou weet of 'n skip die hele pad tot in Indië kon vaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama' (first voyage) and the SAHO and Wikipedia Dias pages: the Portuguese Crown sent the voyage to reach India by sea, for direct access to the spice trade and 'in search of Christians and spices'. 'Wanted to know whether' simplifies that aim without falsifying it, and the block 'Wat dit verander het' supplies the trade motive.

items.bewering: 'n Portugese vloot onder Vasco da Gama het toe verder as Dias gevaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': left Lisbon 8 July 1497 with four ships, passed the Great Fish River (Dias's furthest point) by 16 December 1497, and continued up the East African coast.

items.bewering: Hulle het om die suidpunt en toe noord langs die ooskus van Afrika gevaar. Van daar het hulle oor die Indiese Oseaan gevaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': rounded the Cape, called at Mozambique (March 1498), Mombasa (April) and Malindi (14 April 1498), then crossed the Indian Ocean from Malindi to Kozhikode. Encyclopaedia Britannica 8th ed. (1860, jimclifford.ca transcription) gives the same route.

items.bewering: Hulle het by 'n handelstad aan die weskus van Indië aangekom.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': arrived at Kappadu near Kozhikode (Calicut) on the Malabar Coast (Kerala, India's south-west coast) on 20 May 1498. World History Encyclopedia, 'Indian Ocean Trade before the European Conquest', describes Calicut as a leading trading port and the world's main pepper source.

items.bewering: Nou het 'n seepad van Europa om Afrika tot in Indië geloop.
items.bron: This is an implied 'first' (the first sea route from Europe to India around Africa). Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama', describes the voyage as the first to link Europe and Asia by an ocean route around the southern tip of Africa. No earlier European sea voyage to India is recorded. The wording claims no more than that.

items.bewering: Die Indiese Oseaan was nie 'n leë see nie. Handelaars van Arabië, van Indië en van die Swahili-kus het al eeue lank hier gevaar.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Indian Ocean Trade before the European Conquest' (worldhistory.org/article/1800): Arab traders were active from antiquity, Gujarati and Malabar traders were rivalling Arabs by the late 15th century, and the Swahili city-states (Kilwa, Mombasa, Malindi) were rich trading centres from the 12th to 15th centuries. The network existed 'for centuries'. Also College Board AP Central, 'Indian Ocean world': monsoon trade for two millennia. 'Nie 'n leë see nie' is a metaphor whose mapping holds.

items.bewering: Langs die kuste het hawens en stede gelê waar skepe hul vrag gelaai het.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Indian Ocean Trade before the European Conquest': lists the ports of Aden, Hormuz, Calicut, Cochin, Cambay, Malacca, Sofala, Kilwa, Mombasa, Malindi and Mogadishu, through which goods were shipped.

items.bewering: Da Gama se vloot het by 'n hawe aan die ooskus van Afrika 'n loods aan boord geneem. Daardie loods het die pad oor die oseaan geken en die skepe reg gewys.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': at Malindi (Kenya), da Gama hired a pilot, usually identified as Gujarati, who used his knowledge of the monsoon winds to guide the fleet to Kozhikode. Britannica 8th ed. (1860): 'secured the services of an Indian pilot' at Melinda. The lesson rightly does not name the pilot. The popular attribution to Ibn Majid is rejected by most scholars (Wikipedia, 'Ahmad ibn Majid'; Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal note on David Lopes and Ferrand), so naming him would be a fault.

items.bewering: Die see was dus aan ander mense goed bekend voordat die Portugese daar aangekom het.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: Follows from the two sources above: World History Encyclopedia on centuries of pre-Portuguese Indian Ocean trade, and Wikipedia 'Vasco da Gama' on the local pilot's knowledge of the monsoon route.

items.bewering: Baie jare later het handelaars uit Nederland na die Ooste begin vaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Compagnie van Verre' and 'Dutch East India Company': the Compagnie van Verre was founded in 1594 by Amsterdam merchants, and Cornelis de Houtman's expedition sailed in 1595 and reached Banten. That is about a century after Da Gama (1497-98), so 'baie jare later' is accurate.

items.bewering: Hulle het een groot maatskappy gevorm, die VOC.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company': on 20 March 1602 the States General merged the merchant 'voorcompagnieën' (Compagnie van Verre, Brabantsche Compagnie and others) into the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC). The merger was brokered by the States General (Van Oldenbarnevelt), but the companies were the merchants' own, so 'they formed one company' is a fair simplification.

items.bewering: 'n Ander naam daarvoor is die Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie.
items.bron: Stellenbosch University SUNScholar, 1954 doctoral thesis 'Immigrasie aan die Kaap gedurende die bewind van die Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie' (scholar.sun.ac.za/handle/10019.1/56488) uses exactly this name. It is an Afrikaans counterpart of the English 'Dutch East India Company'. Afrikaans Wikipedia uses 'Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie' (whose initials give VOC) and also 'Nederlandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie'. The lesson says 'another name', not that VOC abbreviates it, so it is correct.

items.bewering: Die VOC het jaar na jaar vlote om die suidpunt van Afrika na die Ooste gestuur.
items.bron: vocwarfare.net (thesis, ch. 3, 'decision-making and the rhythm of the return fleet'): outward ships left in recurring yearly groups (Christmas, Easter, and from the 1630s the Fair fleet), loose groupings rather than strict convoys, and ships sailed almost all year. Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company': 4 785 ships between 1602 and 1796. 'Vlote' (fleets) is acceptable usage.

items.bewering: Op 'n lang reis het vars kos en water opgeraak. Daarom het hulle skepe in Tafelbaai by die Kaap stilgehou vir vars water en kos.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Dutch settlement': in the 1600s Dutch and British ships used the Cape as a halfway stop. Table Bay was chosen for its fresh water, and the 1652 station supplied VOC ships with fresh fruit, vegetables and meat and let crews recover. Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie': Dutch and British ships called regularly at Table Bay before the 1652 refreshment station. The claim holds both before and after 1652.

items.bewering: Die Kaap lê aan die suidweste van Afrika.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Cape of Good Hope': the most south-westerly point of the African continent. The official sign at the site reads the same (Atlas Obscura). The lesson correctly does not call the Cape the southern tip.

items.bewering: om die suidpunt van Afrika (in 'Verder as Dias', 'Die VOC se reise' and in 'In watter orde dit gebeur het')
items.bron: 'Suidpunt' is an implied superlative (the southernmost point). The southernmost point is Cape Agulhas, not the Cape of Good Hope (New World Encyclopedia; SAHO notes Dias passed Cape Agulhas). Dias, Da Gama and VOC ships all sailed around both capes, so 'om die suidpunt' is true in every place it is used. The lesson never equates the Kaap/Tafelbaai with the southern tip.

items.bewering: Eers het Dias om die suidpunt van Afrika en 'n entjie verder langs die kus gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: SAHO, '12 March 1488' (node/10799): Dias was blown round Africa's southernmost tip, landed at Mossel Bay on 3 February 1488, sailed further east, probably turned back at the Great Fish River, and erected the Kwaaihoek padrão on 12 March 1488. Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias', agrees. 'Eers' is correct in the lesson's own sequence: Dias was the first recorded European to round the tip, before Da Gama. 'N entjie verder' (a few hundred km of coast) is fair.

items.bewering: In die 1490's het Da Gama toe die hele pad tot in Indië gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': left Lisbon July 1497 and reached Kozhikode on 20 May 1498. Both dates fall in the 1490s.

items.bewering: Baie later het VOC-vlote gereeld om die suidpunt van Afrika na die Ooste gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company': VOC founded 1602, about a century after Da Gama. vocwarfare.net: recurring yearly fleets. Same sources as the VOC block.

items.bewering: Skepe uit Europa kon nou self speserye en ander goedere in die Ooste gaan haal.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': the Crown sought direct access to the spice trade and to challenge Muslim dominance of Indian Ocean trade. The spices brought back showed the profit potential, and yearly Portuguese India Armadas followed. World History Encyclopedia: before this, goods reached Europe through Aden and Egypt.

items.bewering: Vroeër het min skepe uit Europa tot by die suidpunt gekom.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Dutch settlement': Portuguese ships passed the Cape from 1488. Before 1488 no European ship is recorded there, and before Da Gama only Dias's small expedition (SAHO node/10799; Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias'). 'Min' (few) is therefore true. Note for a human, not a fault: 'min' slightly understates how rare it was, since before Dias it was none. The lesson's own sequence list makes clear that Dias came first.

items.bewering: Nou het die pad om Suider-Afrika 'n gereelde skeepspad geword.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Vasco da Gama': the route was followed by yearly Portuguese India Armadas (Carreira da Índia). Later VOC fleets used it yearly (vocwarfare.net).

items.bewering: VOC: Die groot maatskappy uit Nederland wat skepe na die Ooste gestuur het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company': Dutch chartered company founded in 1602 with a monopoly on Dutch trade in Asia, which sent 4 785 ships between 1602 and 1796. Dictionary of South African English (dsae.co.za, 'VOC'): the Dutch East India Company, Vereenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie.

items.bewering: loods: Iemand wat die see goed ken en 'n skip se pad wys.
items.bron: Wiktionary, 'loods': Afrikaans noun 'navigator, pilot'. Dutch sense: 'pilot, expert who helps navigate to the harbor or coast', and in an extended sense 'guide'. The definition is accurate at this level and fits the Malindi pilot as the lesson uses the word. (Afrikaans 'loods' also means a shed. That sense is not used here.)

items.bewering: vloot: 'n Groep skepe wat saamhoort: hulle het een eienaar, een leier of een soort werk.
items.bron: Wiktionary, 'fleet': 'a group of vessels ... generally operating in a unified way or traveling together', including those owned commercially by one company and ships in company under naval command. Dutch 'vloot': 'bij elkaar horende schepen', with derived forms handelsvloot and vissersvloot. Merriam-Webster (via search): 'a group of warships under a single command' and 'a group of ships ... operated under unified control', with fishing fleet as an example. The three alternatives (owner, leader, kind of work) each map to an attested sense.

opsomming: All 26 checkable claims hold up against sources, including the implied superlatives ('suidpunt', the implied first sea route, 'eers'), the 'halfpad' road metaphor and the three glossary definitions. Nothing needs correcting. Worth a human's glance only: 'min skepe' before Da Gama is true (only Dias's expedition), and 'Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie' is an attested Afrikaans name but not the name the initials VOC stand for, which the lesson does not claim.
